To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
combined inactivation of rb 1 and rbl 1 is required and sufficient for the development of retinoblastomata, small cell pancreatic neuroendocrine carcinomas and glioblastoma.
Rbl1 functions as tumor suppressors in high-grade glioblastoma, choroid plexuspapilloma, and small-cell pancreas neuroendocrine carcinoma.
RBL1 functions as tumor suppressors in glioblastomas, small-cell pancreatic neuroendo-crine carcinomas, and choroid plexuspapillomas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the retinolblastoma and p53 signaling network in tumorigenesis.

the development and use of CRISPR/CAS9 technology in Xenopus to generate novel models of human cancer, which can then be used to study the functional role of tumor suppressor genes in cancer development.
the role of the retinoblstoma protein family and p53 in tumorigenesis, and the functional redundancy within this family in suppressing tumorigenicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Rbl1 functions as tumor suppressors in SC-PaNECs and glioma/gioblastoma, and that the Rb1 and Rbl1 proteins function as tumor suppressors with functional redundancy.
Rbl1 functions as tumor suppresser in both SC-PaNECs and glioblastoma, but that it is not sufficient to drive SCLC in X. tropicalis.
Rbl1 acts as a tumor suppressor in X. tropicalis, and is a key player in the RB1-p53 tumor suppressor network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the retinoblastic proteins are tumor suppressors, but that they have a different role in different tumors.
Rbl1 functions as tumor suppressors in both SC-PaNECs and gliomas, but that it has little impact on the development of SCLCs.
RBL1 (p105) acts as a tumor suppressor in the context of RB1 loss, and in the context of TP53 loss, in the context of glioblastoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Rb1 and Rbl1 are both required for suppressing the formation and progression of SC-PaNeC.

combined inactivation of rb and rbl1 is required and sufficient for the induction of small-cell pancreatic neuro-endocrine carcinoma and astrocytomas/glioblastomas, while inactivation of tp is required and sufficient in the latter.
combined inactivation of Rb1 and Rbl1, and possibly Rbl2, is required and sufficient for the development of SC-PaNeC, retinblastoma, and astrocytomas.
